content.text: The key gap is now clear: `research_tender`, `research_spec`, `research_mail`, and ERP research produce typed facts, while `solve()` does not call them or join their results for `calculate()`. I’m writing a worktree-only design that makes each fact’s source explicit and shows the dependency chain into submission.

input.input:
const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /private/tmp/error404ai-critical-path/docs/critical-path.md
+# Critical path and source routing
+
+This is a design for the isolated `codex/critical-path` worktree, based on the code at
+`b81e8a3`. It does not change the running agent.
+
+## What runs today
+
+`agent/agent.py:solve` reads a `Briefing`, opens the bid and mail sites, and calls
+`submit_bid` without an answer. The form therefore omits every position. The research
+functions and the calculation exist, but `solve` does not call them. In particular,
+`research_sites`, `research_tender`, `research_spec`, `research_mail`, `Erp.requirement`,
+`bid_clauses`, `to_position_input`, and `calculate` are not connected to the entry point.
+
+## The critical path for a complete bid
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+  B[Brief and access list] --> R[Bind site roles and source map]
+  R --> T[Tender positions and Q&A]
+  R --> S[Current specification revision and requirements]
+  R --> M[Authority mail records]
+  T --> J[Join position to requirement]
+  S --> J
+  T --> E[Apply amendments]
+  S --> E
+  M --> E
+  E --> P[ERP catalogue group search and material details]
+  P --> C[Build BidInput and calculate]
+  T --> C
+  M --> C
+  C --> F[Enter form and check review]
+  F --> N[Request current TAN from mail]
+  N --> X[Sign and confirm]
+```
+
+The longest serial dependency is **brief → site binding → current specification →
+effective requirement → ERP match and prices → calculation → form → TAN →
+confirmation**. Tender positions and Q&A must be joined before calculation and
+amendments before final material selection. Most mail research can run alongside
+tender/spec research. The TAN is deliberately last because requesting a new one
+invalidates the previous one.
+
+## Tell the agent where facts live
+
+Create a per-run `SourceMap` from the brief and `access` list. The map is a dispatch
+contract, not an answer cache: it identifies **which site and record class** can
+establish a fact. The run can rename site IDs and split sites differently, so bind
+roles from brief evidence at runtime and reject unknown IDs. A model may extract
+role labels from the brief once; downstream workers should receive only their assigned
+site and exact research goal. They should never choose a site from all available sites.
+
+| Fact needed | Assigned source | Existing reader or resolver |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Tender reference, scenario date, bidder identity, site roles | Brief and access list | `briefing.read_brief`; `research.research_sites` for spec/ERP |
+| Positions, original quantities, requirement IDs | Tender documents on bid site | `research_tender.research_tender` |
+| Quantity changes, withdrawals, condition and tariff keys, amendments | Tender Q&A on bid site | `research_tender.resolve_tender` |
+| Governing revision, dimensions, catalogue group, pieces per set | Specification site | `research.research_spec` |
+| Approval, reserves, FX, index, packaging, delivery, pool, bonus rules | Authorised records on assigned mail/authority site | `research_mail.plan_searches`, `research_mail.research_mail`, `research_mail.resolve_mail` |
+| Candidate material, active status, stock, lead times, price conditions | ERP site, searched by **catalogue group from the requirement** | `research.Erp.requirement` and `Erp.material` |
+| Effective attributes and exact material match | Prior typed facts | `evidence.effective_requirement`, `check_choice`, `research.reselect` |
+| Quantity, unit price, discount, total | Prior typed facts | `research_mail.bid_clauses`, `evidence.to_position_input`, `calc.calculate` |
+| Signing TAN | Webmail after form review | `submit.Mailbox.tan` inside `submit_bid` |
+
+This gives a deterministic route for each fact type. A worker still needs to read
+the assigned site's actual pages, choose the current revision, and find the right
+record; page layouts and record identities vary. The code already validates exact
+reference, sender and scenario date for mail; Q&A resolution applies dates and
+withdrawals; ERP choice checks active status and attribute equality. Keep these as
+gates after extraction. Add source URL/document ID, revision, page or message ID,
+and observed timestamp to each fact so the join can explain and audit its inputs.
+
+## Smallest useful orchestration
+
+1. **Bootstrap:** read the brief and bind `bid`, `mail`, `spec`, and `erp` site IDs.
+   Validate that required roles are present and distinct where the brief requires it.
+   Build the source map from those roles and the known fact classes. The current
+   `plan_searches` can extract subject/sender/schema from the brief, but its site
+   choice is still a model output; constrain it to the mapped authority site(s).
+2. **Parallel research:** start tender, spec, and authority mail research on their
+   assigned sessions. `research_spec` can emit each requirement as soon as it is
+   parsed and warm ERP after the revision is selected.
+3. **Per requirement:** join by the tender's requirement ID. Apply Q&A amendments and
+   mail reserves to create `EffectiveRequirement`. Search the ERP with its catalogue
+   group, inspect candidates, then select or reselect after pending facts arrive.
+4. **Join gate:** require every tender position to have a matching current-revision
+   requirement and resolved material or an explicit failure. Check the required mail
+   clauses, condition validity, stock/lead time and pricing inputs. Record missing
+   facts instead of silently filling defaults that imply a valid bid.
+5. **Pure calculation and action:** construct `BidInput`, call `calculate`, pass
+   `BidResult.answer()` plus chosen material attributes to `submit_bid`. Check the
+   review page, request the TAN, sign, and verify the site's confirmation. Reserve
+   the existing 90-second safety margin for this tail.
+
+This can be written as a small `asyncio` coordinator with typed state and explicit
+join gates. A LangGraph graph could represent the same nodes and conditional edges,
+but its main benefit here would be persisted state, resumability and visual traces.
+It would not solve source selection. Introduce it only if interrupted runs or
+branching retries become a demonstrated problem; `docs/plan.md` already records the
+dependency and debugging cost of adding it to this project.
+
+## First executable slice
+
+Wire one position end to end behind the existing entry point in this worktree:
+brief → source map → tender/spec → effective requirement → ERP → `BidInput` →
+`calculate` → `submit_bid`. Run it without signing first, using the existing
+`AGENT_STOP_BEFORE_SIGN` switch, and inspect the trace plus form review. Then add
+parallel mail clauses, all positions, and the final signing path. The first slice
+should assert that the source map never dispatches a fact to an unassigned site,
+that every joined requirement belongs to the chosen revision, and that missing
+required evidence blocks calculation or marks the position unresolved.
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

content.text:
Yes. The critical path is **brief → site and source map → current specification and tender facts → effective requirement → ERP material and price → calculation → bid form → TAN → confirmation**. Mail research can run alongside the tender and specification work.

The main finding is that the research and calculation pieces exist, but `solve()` does not connect them; it currently submits a bid with omitted positions. A per-run source map could tell each worker which site and record type holds its facts, leaving the LLM to navigate and read within that assigned source. LangGraph could represent the flow, but it would not itself solve source routing.

I wrote the traced flow, fact-to-source table, and a first implementation slice in [critical-path.md](</private/tmp/error404ai-critical-path/docs/critical-path.md>). It is in the separate `codex/critical-path` worktree. The current checkout is unchanged; this was a design pass, so no runtime test was run.
